q: The notion of computational depth (logical depth, Bennett 1988) measures the computational effort needed to produce a string. A string x has high logical depth if:
opts: The shortest program for x takes many steps to run (deep = costly to compute but short to describe)
x has high mutual information with the halting string Ω
exp: Logical depth: x has depth d if the shortest program of length ≤ K(x)+c takes ≥ d steps to output x. Deep objects (like Mandelbrot set images, evolved organisms) are 'information-dense': their structure took long to compute even if the description is short.
